reason: The time-machine console display and operating controls face the viewer while the character stands behind it, violating the explicit prop-facing-character requirement. This is a source direction defect, not a keying issue.

defects.description: The screen and buttons are presented toward camera; the character behind the unit would look at its back instead of the console face.

inspection_scope.technical_scope: Existing native240 boundary gate reused, not rerun. Source and evidence manifest are SHA-bound.
limits: Representative source stills only, not all243 manually inspected.
No continuous source video playback in this source stage; complete10s playback is reserved for final candidate QA.
No automatic final-media approval or repair.

visual_findings: Complete headwear and shoes remain visible in representative frames.
The tiny red antenna is visibly handled, but the control face and screen are on the camera-facing side. Named upper-body performance does not waive the prop orientation requirement.
No attempt was made to rotate, repaint or erase the generated console.
